stories.title: Bow River Inks $53.9M Acquisition Loan for Northlake Apartment Sale
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged $53.9 million in financing for the acquisition of Dry Creek Ranch, a 456-unit multifamily community in Northlake, Texas. Bow River Capital purchased the asset from Western Securities. Newmark’s Adam Randall, John Westby-Gibson and Drake Blodgett arranged the five-year, fixed-rate, full-term interest-only Fannie Mae loan on behalf of the Bow River. Located on approximately 29 acres, Dry Creek Ranch offers a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom residences with amenities including multiple swimming pools, a fitness center, clubhouse, business center and recreational facilities. The community is near AllianceTexas, Charles Schwab’s regional headquarters, Fidelity Investments’ Westlake campus and other major employment centers, with convenient access to Interstate 35W, State Highway 114 and DFW International Airport. Bow River Capital acquired Dry Creek Ranch through its BRC Multi-Family Dislocation Fund, which focuses on existing, cash-flowing apartment communities across growth-oriented Midwest and Southwest markets. The post Bow River Inks $53.9M Acquisition Loan for Northlake Apartment Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bow River Capital acquired 456-unit Dry Creek Ranch in Northlake, TX via $53.9M Fannie Mae loan.
Property near Charles Schwab HQ, Fidelity Westlake campus, and DFW Airport; mixed 1/2/3-bed units.
Fixed-rate, full-term interest-only financing signals strong fundamentals in North Texas multifamily corridor.
stories.summary: Bow River Capital purchased Dry Creek Ranch, a 456-unit apartment community in Northlake, Texas, through a $53.9 million five-year fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan arranged by Newmark. The 29-acre property sits near major employers including Charles Schwab's regional headquarters and Fidelity's Westlake campus, with direct access to I-35W and DFW International Airport. The acquisition aligns with Bow River's focus on cash-flowing assets in growth-oriented Southwest markets.
stories.impact: Northlake's proximity to major corporate campuses (Schwab, Fidelity) and DFW logistics hubs signals sustained employment clustering and population inflow; strong debt pricing (fixed-rate, interest-only) reflects lender confidence in the North Texas multifamily fundamentals despite broader rate environment. Developers should monitor secondary locations along I-35W corridor as satellite office/logistics growth continues to support rental demand.

stories.title: Hunt Sports Unveils New Frisco “Year-Round Destination”
stories.excerpt: Hunt Sports Development is partnering with Peak Curated Development and Venu Holding Corporation on a mixed-use district on the east side of Toyota Stadium and Soccer Center in Frisco, the home of FC Dallas. The district will feature more than one million square feet of premium office space. The partnership will transform the campus into a year-round destination for hospitality, business, dining, and entertainment. The project is slated for groundbreaking in 2027. The first phase of the project will feature an approximately 290-room boutique hotel and more than 40,000 square feet of convention, meeting and event space. The hotel will have a full-service restaurant and bar, a rooftop bar and lounge, and an experiential spa and fitness center. It will include a flexible convention and event center featuring more than 25,000 square feet of dedicated meeting space, including a 15,000-square-foot ballroom. The $215 million renovation to Toyota Stadium is on schedule for completion in the spring of 2028. The post Hunt Sports Unveils New Frisco “Year-Round Destination” appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hunt Sports, Peak Curated, Venu developing 1M+ SF mixed-use district at FC Dallas campus, Frisco.
Phase 1: 290-room boutique hotel, 40K SF event space, restaurants, spa; groundbreaking 2027.
Toyota Stadium $215M renovation on track for spring 2028; transforms suburban sports venue into year-round destination.
stories.summary: Hunt Sports Development is partnering with Peak Curated Development and Venu Holding to build a mixed-use district on Frisco's east side anchored by FC Dallas's Toyota Stadium. The first phase includes a 290-room boutique hotel with 40,000 square feet of convention and event space, full-service restaurant, rooftop bar, and spa. Groundbreaking is slated for 2027, with a $215 million stadium renovation completing in spring 2028.
stories.impact: The multi-year timeline and large-scale hospitality/office development signal a broader strategy to densify around sports anchors in North Texas suburbs; the project will drive daytime employment concentration and overnight visitor volume in Frisco. Developers should assess whether the hospitality-office-dining mix creates spillover demand for nearby residential (workforce housing) or if it remains isolated from residential multifamily submarkets.

stories.title: Investicore Acquires 14-Building Charlotte Office Complex
stories.excerpt: Investicore Holdings purchased a 14-building 568,811-square-foot Charlotte complex for $64 million. Ares was the seller. The Charlotte Business Journal reports the 42-acre park, called ThExchange, is 60% occupied. One building is entirely vacant. Investicore plans to convert part of one of the buildings into a food-and-beverage area. John Vickers of KW Commercial brokered the acquisition for Investicore. Matt Smith and Patrick Gildea of CBRE brokered it for Ares. The park was listed for sale in April. A KW Commercial team led by Vickers will handle leasing efforts at ThExchange. The owner prior to Ares, The Dilweg Cos., spent about $34 million and two years overhauling the property. Those renovations were completed in 2020. The Dilweg Cos. turned the property over to Ares in 2024 after its $68.6 million loan matured and became nonperforming. The post Investicore Acquires 14-Building Charlotte Office Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Investicore acquired 568K-SF, 14-building ThExchange office park in Charlotte for $64M; 60% occupied.
Ares seller after $68.6M nonperforming loan matured in 2024; Dilweg spent $34M renovating through 2020.
Value-add play: 1 vacant building, F&B conversion planned; low basis in distressed sale suggests soft office market.
stories.summary: Investicore Holdings purchased ThExchange, a 568,811-square-foot, 14-building office complex in Charlotte, from Ares for $64 million. The 42-acre park is currently 60% occupied with one entirely vacant building. Ares acquired the property after the prior owner's $68.6 million loan became nonperforming in 2024, despite extensive renovations completed in 2020. Investicore plans to convert part of one building into food-and-beverage space.
stories.impact: Charlotte office distress and poor absorption post-renovation signal limited demand for traditional flex/corporate space; the sharp markdown from Dilweg's $34M investment to Investicore's $64M acquisition reflects structural office weakness. Multifamily developers should note: softening office fundamentals in Charlotte may weaken white-collar migration tailwinds and reduce renter quality/income stability. Monitor concurrent multifamily absorption and rent growth to confirm whether office weakness is bleeding into residential markets.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Land Palm City Development Marketing Assignment
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has been selected by Mattamy Homes to market the multifamily development component in Downtown Newfield and the broader master-planned community’s Workplace District, which includes retail, flex and warehouse space, in Newfield, Mattamy’s master-planned community in Palm City, Florida.The marketing assignment is being led by Nikolaus Schroth and James McKinney of Cushman & Wakefield’s Stuart, Florida, office.Newfield is a 3,400-acre “agrihood” master-planned community. The community is planned for approximately 4,200 residences, more than 100,000 square feet of retail and dining space and a growing employment base anchored by a planned 2 million-square-foot Workplace District. As for Newfield’s multifamily component, the three opportunities available to one or multiple development partners include 414 planned residential units within a walkable town center environment designed to integrate housing, shopping, dining, recreation and employment uses. bullets: Mattamy Homes marketing 414 multifamily units in Downtown Newfield, Palm City agrihood master plan.
3,400-acre community planned for ~4,200 residences, 100K+ SF retail, flex, warehouse; walkable town center model.
Cushman & Wakefield (Stuart office) leading leasing; mixed-use/retail/workplace district positioned as integrated employment hub.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield has been assigned to market the multifamily development component of Newfield, a 3,400-acre master-planned agrihood community in Palm City, Florida. The marketing initiative covers 414 planned residential units in a walkable downtown environment integrated with retail, dining, recreation, and employment uses. The broader Newfield campus includes 100,000+ square feet of retail, flex, and warehouse space designated as a Workplace District.
stories.impact: The 'agrihood' positioning and employment-embedded model may signal demand for lifestyle-oriented suburban housing in South Florida; however, the scale (414 units) and soft-lease status suggest this is early-stage, pre-construction development. The Workplace District integration is a supply-side headwind if it cannibalizes local office demand or if the project struggles to attract anchor employers. Developers should assess whether similar mixed-use agrihood models can sustain pricing power in Palm City's competitive rental market.

stories.title: Corcoran Sunshine Marketing Group’s Kelly Kennedy Mack Can’t Slow Down
stories.excerpt: Manhattan native Kelly Kennedy Mack, president of Corcoran Sunshine Marketing Group since 2006, had been to Europe around 20 times already by the time she was 10 years old. Growing up in Peter Cooper Village with a father who was a sales and marketing executive for Pan Am, it now seems clear that Mack was destined to be constantly on the go. “I love to travel. Now that I have children, I love to take them traveling whenever we can,” said Mack, 52, who lives in Midtown West with her husband, Stephen Mack, co-founder and managing partner of Solon Mack Capital, and their two daughters, ages 7 and 9. “[As kids], my sister and I were always adaptable. We always had the ability to make new relationships and meet new people. We were around a lot of grown-ups and a lot of different cultures and ideas. We went everywhere.” This wanderlust translates to her current everyday life in New York City, which can find her walking five to seven miles a day checking on her various residential projects. Corcoran Sunshine Marketing Group’s internal tracking of Manhattan residential sales places it at No. 1 among firms specializing in marketing and selling newly built homes, with sales of around $3 billion each year from 2021 through 2025 and over $65 billion in sales over the life of the company. Its work on Hudson Yards alone resulted in 428 sales totaling over $2.5 billion, according to the firm. Mack estimates that the company represents around 30 to 40 projects at any one time, and that so far in 2026 it has represented around 40 percent of the sponsor sales in Manhattan by dollar volume. stories.title: Trump, Mamdani Advance Sunnyside Yards Housing Discussion
stories.excerpt: President Donald Trump and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani forged common ground Monday to advance an affordable housing plan at an Amtrak-controlled train yard in Sunnyside, Queens. Mamdani and Trump said in a Monday evening press conference after meeting at Gracie Mansion that dialogue will continue on avenues to get federal approvals for long-stalled plans to build 12,000 affordable housing units over Sunnyside Yards. “We’ve agreed to set up a new level of that conversation between our housing and operations team at City Hall and the White House team,” Mamdani said at the press conference while standing beside Trump outside Gracie Mansion. “We are sincerely interested and committed to this as an idea, which is why it’s been the focus of the conversations I’ve had with the president.” Monday’s meeting came nearly seven months after Mamdani met with Trump at the White House in late February and asked for $21 billion in federal grants to fund a platform for the housing project. The Sunnyside Yard development would include 12,000 housing units, half funded by New York State’s Mitchell-Lama affordable housing program, along with parks and schools. The plan was first pitched under then-Mayor Bill de Blasio’s administration and widely opposed by local residents. “I would say that it’s a very federal-oriented job,” Trump said at the press conference. “You’re going to need a lot of federal approvals and probably some federal money to do it. But it’s always been a great location.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Trump, NYC Mayor Mamdani advance federal approval for 12,000 affordable units at Amtrak's Sunnyside Yards, Queens.
Mamdani requested $21B federal grants for infrastructure platform; new White House–City Hall working group formed.
Multi-year stall on Amtrak-controlled site; dialogue signals potential unlocking of major supply in tight Queens market.
stories.summary: President Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced agreement to advance a long-stalled affordable housing project at Sunnyside Yards in Queens, aiming to build 12,000 units over the Amtrak-controlled rail yard. Mamdani had previously requested $21 billion in federal grants for the platform infrastructure. A new working group between City Hall and the White House will continue discussions on federal approvals and funding mechanisms.
stories.impact: Sunnyside Yards represents a potential step-change in Queens affordable supply (12,000 units is significant) if federal funding and Amtrak cooperation materialize; however, the multi-year dialogue history and infrastructure complexity create substantial execution risk. For market-rate multifamily developers: a large affordable project in Queens could depress rents in the western outer boroughs if priced aggressively, or could increase local employment and improve transit access, supporting broader rental demand. Monitor federal appropriations and White House timelines before assuming supply impact.

stories.title: Investor Buys Montgomery Hyundai Plant, Adding 240K-SF
stories.excerpt: PRP Real Assets acquired the newly-built Hyundai-Mobis Class-A, Flagship Redistribution Center in Montgomery, AL for $66.5 million. The property is leased to Hyundai for 14 years and guaranteed by Hyundai-Mobis. PRP Real Assets has also agreed to provide an additional $30 million in funding to expand the facility’s footprint by over 240,000 square feet. Serving over 2,000 dealers nationwide and encompassing over 450,000 square feet of Class-A, mission-critical logistics space, the Montgomery, AL facility is the primary redistribution center for Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis aftermarket service parts in the United States. The property was delivered in September of 2025 on a 60-acre site. The site is fully integrated within Hyundai’s broader 1.6 million-square-foot campus in Montgomery, AL and is fully entitled for significant expansion. Hyundai-Mobis, who occupies 100% of the building, has committed $26 billion to United States operations through 2028 and is increasing domestic manufacturing capacity by 64%, the largest expansion announced by a foreign automaker in the current cycle. The 450,000-square-foot facility serves as the primary redistribution hub for Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis aftermarket parts nationwide. PRP has committed an additional $30 million to expand the facility by over 240,000 square feet; Hyundai-Mobis has pledged $26 billion in U.S. operations through 2028 and is increasing domestic manufacturing capacity by 64%, the largest foreign automaker expansion in the current cycle.
stories.impact: Hyundai's massive capital commitment and 64% manufacturing-capacity expansion in Montgomery signals sustained employment growth and supply-chain clustering in central Alabama. This tier-1 logistics investment will drive wage growth for blue-collar and supervisory workers, supporting rental demand for workforce housing in Montgomery and nearby markets. Developers should target workforce multifamily (Class B/C, 2–3 bed) in proximity to the Hyundai campus and I-65 corridor; the 14-year lease and expansion entitlement signal 10+ years of operational stability and job creation tailwinds.

stories.title: Vikas Enti of Reframe Systems: 5 Questions

Energy Impact Partners led the round, as Reframe aims to apply robotics, software and regional microfactories — which are exactly what they sound like — to an industrialized homebuilding model it said is capable of delivering homes up to three times faster and at more than 35 percent lower cost than traditional construction. Co-founder and CEO Vikas Enti leads Reframe. He’s a mechanical engineer and former Amazon Robotics executive who spent 11 years helping scale more than 500,000 robots across the e-commerce giant’s fulfillment network. Last week, Commercial Observer spoke with Enti about his company’s AI- and robotics-driven microfactories and how they can help build a variety of quality homes globally. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Reframe has been operating since 2022, but why the recent $40 million funding? Vikas Enti: We’re a physical AI company where our whole mission is to solve for housing. How do we make housing abundant and resilient? We’ve developed a technology and a business strategy for building housing in microfactories and building a network of these microfactories around the world that produce homes that are all electric, low-embodied carbon and net zero energy by default. The recent fundraise is part of our growth activities. We have a healthy backlog of customers we’re building toward and that requires us to expand capacity — to move from our prototype-scale microfactory here in Andover, Mass., called Fab Zero, to Fab One, which is our production-scale microfactory in Billerica, Mass. bullets: Reframe Systems raised $40M (Energy Impact Partners lead) to scale microfactory home manufacturing.
AI/robotics platform claims 3x faster delivery, 35%+ cost reduction vs. traditional construction.
MA-based company applies industrialized homebuilding model; implications for construction cost, feasibility, supply pipeline.
stories.summary: Massachusetts-based Reframe Systems, a physical AI and robotics housing company, raised $40 million led by Energy Impact Partners to expand its microfactory manufacturing model. Co-founder and CEO Vikas Enti, a former Amazon Robotics executive, leads the company's effort to apply robotics, software, and regional microfactories to industrialized homebuilding. Reframe claims its model can deliver homes up to three times faster and at more than 35 percent lower cost than traditional construction methods.
stories.impact: If Reframe's cost/speed claims materialize at scale, industrialized home manufacturing could materially reduce single-family and multifamily construction costs and timelines, improving development feasibility in cost-constrained markets. However, this technology is pre-scale (founded 2022, early capital raise); developers should monitor adoption rates and actual delivered-project economics over the next 12–18 months. A successful scaling could compress construction pricing power and accelerate supply delivery in high-cost metros, threatening value-add development timing.

stories.title: Ian Michael Klein, Rabina’s Development Head, Wanted to Be ‘a Real Estate Guy’
stories.excerpt: When Ian Michael Klein, head of development and construction at Rabina, told his dad — a commercial real estate broker — that he wanted to go into architecture, his dad didn’t really see the draw. To the elder Klein, architecture was all about square feet, but to the son it was so much more. Klein, 43, graduated from Cornell University in 2005 with a degree in architecture and an intent to get into development, and what he admits was a somewhat naive idea of how to get that done. “I tried to get a job in real estate development, but nobody would hire me,” he said. “I would approach developers and they’d say, ‘Well, you’re an architect’ and I’d say, ‘No, I’m a real estate guy,’ and they’d say, ‘This piece of paper says you’re an architect.’ So it took me a minute to get into development.” Eventually, Klein found a job working for a small architect who had a real estate development practice and who mentored him about the real estate side of things to help facilitate that transition. Fast forward to 2010 — the year Klein earned a master’s in architecture and urban design at Harvard — and he is a senior project manager at the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) during the Bloomberg administration. There he was part of a team that was structuring all of the public-private transactions throughout the city, helping the administration decide what can and should be built in certain areas, and finding developers to get the job done. While with the NYCEDC, Klein worked on some massive projects. stories.title: Adam America, JW Capital Land $180M Refi for Florida International Student Housing
stories.excerpt: The owners of a student housing property adjacent to Florida International University have secured a $180 million refinancing, Commercial Observer can first report. Adam America Real Estate and JW Capital Management landed the financing for Terrazul, their 1,201-bed asset in Miami-Dade County. Corebridge Financial provided the loan, which will retire the 22-story property’s existing construction financing and return cash-out proceeds to the joint venture. Terrazul was completed in 2024 at 700 Southwest 107th Avenue in Sweetwater. The property includes 932 units totaling 1,201 beds, 647 parking spaces and 15,442 square feet of ground-floor retail. It is currently 98 percent occupied, according to the ownership group. “Terrazul has demonstrated the strength of the FIU student housing market and the quality of the asset we developed alongside JW Capital Management,” Adam America CEO David Brickman said in a statement. He added that the refinancing allows the partners to realize value from the property while continuing to pursue investments in high-growth markets. Terrazul is directly across from FIU’s east entrance and includes studios as well as one-, two- and four-bedroom units. Amenities include an indoor-outdoor rooftop study lounge, conference rooms and library spaces, a fitness center and a resort-style pool. FIU enrolls nearly 60,000 undergraduate, graduate and doctoral students, while the University of Miami is approximately 7 miles southeast from the property. Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory arranged the financing, led by Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer and Michael Ianno. The deal also extends Adam America and JW Capital’s student housing partnership. The firms are planning a 30-story student housing tower near the University of Texas at Austin, while Adam America has previously completed projects near Yale University and the University at Albany. stories.summary: Adam America Real Estate and JW Capital Management secured a $180 million refinancing for Terrazul, a 1,201-bed student housing property in Sweetwater, Florida, adjacent to Florida International University. The 22-story, 932-unit asset, completed in 2024, is currently 98 percent occupied and includes 647 parking spaces and 15,442 square feet of ground-floor retail. Corebridge Financial provided the loan, which retired construction financing and returned cash-out proceeds to the ownership group.
stories.impact: Rapid delivery-to-refinance and 98% occupancy at a new 1,200-bed FIU asset signals strong institutional student housing demand in Miami-Dade and validates the FIU submarkets's ability to absorb large, newly-delivered purpose-built student housing. The cash-out refinance (before typical 3–5 year stabilization window) reflects lender confidence and suggests cap-rate compression in this niche. Multifamily developers should monitor competing student housing supply at FIU and nearby universities; if oversupply materializes, it may depress occupancy and rate growth, particularly for B/C-class conventional multifamily competing for post-grad renters in the Sweetwater corridor.
